original_question: Let L_{p,q} be the Lorentz space on the unit circle T for 1 <= q <= p < infinity, and let H[L_{p,q}] be the associated Hardy-Lorentz space. Determine a nontrivial lower bound for the bounded compact approximation constant M(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M(H[L_{p,q}]) <= 2. Also, for 1 < q <= p < infinity, determine a nontrivial lower bound for the dual compact approximation constant M*(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M*(H[L_{p,q}]) <= 2.
target_in_paper: Open problem 5.8 in Section 5.5 ("Estimates for M and M* in the case of Lorentz spaces").
correct_elements: The draft already captures the correct open problem from the paper: it uses the unweighted Lorentz spaces L_{p,q} on the unit circle, the corresponding Hardy-Lorentz spaces H[L_{p,q}], the correct parameter range 1 ≤ q ≤ p < ∞ for the BCAP question, the correct narrower range 1 < q ≤ p < ∞ for the DCAP question, and the exact currently stated upper bounds M(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2 and M*(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2.
missing_details: It does not define the Lorentz space L_{p,q}(T) explicitly via the non-increasing rearrangement f* and the norm ||f||_{p,q} = (∫_0^1 [t^{1/p} f*(t)]^q dt/t)^{1/q}.
It does not specify the ambient measure space: the unit circle T with normalized Lebesgue measure, and measurable complex-valued functions.
It does not define the Hardy-Lorentz space H[L_{p,q}] as the subspace of L_{p,q}(T) consisting of functions whose negative Fourier coefficients vanish.
It does not say what M(X) and M*(X) mean: the optimal constants in the bounded compact approximation property and dual compact approximation property, respectively.

It does not indicate that the bounds M(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2 and M*(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2 are precisely the Lorentz-specialized bounds (5.9) and (5.10), obtained from the general abstract-Hardy-space result of Theorem 1.3 / Theorem 3.3.

It omits the paper's motivating comparison with the classical case q = p, where L_{p,p} is isometrically isomorphic to L^p and the sharper estimate M(H[L_{p,p}]), M*(H[L_{p,p}]) ≤ 2^{|1-2/p|} is known.
refined_question: Let T be the unit circle endowed with normalized Lebesgue measure. For 1 ≤ q ≤ p < ∞, let L_{p,q}(T) be the Lorentz space of measurable complex-valued functions f on T with norm ||f||_{p,q} = (∫_0^1 [t^{1/p} f*(t)]^q dt/t)^{1/q}, where f* is the non-increasing rearrangement of f, and let H[L_{p,q}] = {f ∈ L_{p,q}(T) : hat f(n) = 0 for all n < 0} be the corresponding Hardy-Lorentz space. Determine a nontrivial lower bound for the optimal bounded compact approximation constant M(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2. In addition, for 1 < q ≤ p < ∞, determine a nontrivial lower bound for the optimal dual compact approximation constant M*(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M*(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2.
justification: This is exactly the Lorentz-space open problem posed in Section 5.5 as Open problem 5.8. The nearby context first defines the Lorentz spaces L_{p,q}, notes that L_{p,p} is isometrically isomorphic to L^p, records the bounds M(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2 and M*(H[L_{p,q}]) ≤ 2 in (5.9)-(5.10), and then states Open problem 5.8 in essentially the same terms as the draft. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must also import from the introduction the definitions of H[X], M(X), and M*(X). The draft is therefore already very close to the paper's exact intent, but it relies on implicit notation and background that the paper supplies in Section 1 and immediately before Open problem 5.8.
